issues.body:
This PR adds `--features hdt,federation,odrl,forms` to the bundle command and adds a new comment saying the build 'enables the native capabilities promised by the desktop release: HDT import, SERVICE federation, ODRL policy previews, and SHACL-derived forms.'

About 20 lines below, in the same comment block for the same step, the pre-existing sq-3w29b paragraph was left untouched and still reads: 'release bundles explicitly enable the native HDT importer, federated SERVICE client, and ODRL policy tool. These native capabilities stay off for lean development builds; Forms remains opt-in until a release explicitly selects its larger SHACL model stack.'

The second half of that sentence is now false: this release DOES explicitly select forms. A reader of the step comment gets two contradictory statements about whether the shipped installer contains the forms bridge or its rebuild stub. Given this repo's PROVEN-vs-DOCUMENTED discipline and the fact that release.yml is tag-only (so nothing else corrects the reader), the stale clause should not survive.
issues.fix_hint:
Update the sq-3w29b paragraph to match reality, e.g.:

    # [SONNET-4.6] sq-3w29b: release bundles explicitly enable the native HDT importer,
    # federated SERVICE client, ODRL policy tool, and SHACL-derived forms bridge. All four
    # stay OFF for lean development builds; the release opts in deliberately (sq-b1hdb).

Also drop the now-redundant duplicate sentence so the block states the enabled feature set exactly once.
issues.title: Self-contradicting comment: the block now says the release enables forms, but the sq-3w29b paragraph below still says forms is not selected

issues.body:
Carried over from round 3, unaddressed. The step asserts only the ABSENCE of 'rebuild (the )?desktop app with'. I confirmed all four current stubs match, so the guard is correct today and is not vacuous in principle (in a lean build the stub fns are reachable from their registered Tauri commands, so the literals survive into .rodata even under lto=true).

But nothing mechanically ties the four source strings to this regex. If any stub is reworded (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89), or a fifth optional capability lands with different wording, or a stub message becomes non-literal via `format!`, the grep finds nothing and the step passes green while the stub ships. Because release.yml is tag-triggered, that drift would never surface on a PR — it would surface as a silently degraded installer.

The added comment naming the four files helps a human but enforces nothing.
issues.fix_hint:
Add a POSITIVE control in the PR-visible lane so the two checks are a matched pair. In gui.yml's `tauri-build` job, after the default-feature `cargo build`, assert the sentinel IS present in the lean binary:

    - name: Sentinel present in lean build (guards release.yml's capability check)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        grep -aEq 'rebuild (the )?desktop app with' target/debug/sparq-gui \
          || { echo 'stub wording drifted; release.yml capability grep is now vacuous' >&2; exit 1; }

Then a reword turns the PR lane red instead of silently disarming the tag-time guard.
issues.title: Capability guard is still negative-only: nothing pins the stub sentinel, so a reword silently disarms it

issues.body:
The amended text reads: 'The native capability feature set (`hdt,federation,odrl,forms`) is clippied and tested in debug mode by gui.yml's ADVISORY (non-gating) tauri-build job. ... the combined-state tests exercise the federation, ODRL, and forms paths.' The previous version said 'tested in debug mode on Linux'.

In gui.yml the union CLIPPY now runs on all five rows (the `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` guard was removed) and each individual feature gets its own clippy+test on all rows, so 'clippied and tested' is substantively true. But the combined-state test still carries `if: runner.os == 'Linux'`, so the unqualified 'the combined-state tests exercise ...' now overstates platform coverage for the macOS/Windows rows.

This does not undermine the `soft: false` decision for the two Linux rows (those ARE covered by the Linux-only combined test), which is why this is minor rather than major — but the qualifier should not have been dropped.
issues.fix_hint:
Restore the qualifier on the sentence that needs it:

    #   * The native capability feature set (`hdt,federation,odrl,forms`) is clippied on every
    #     row and each feature is tested individually by gui.yml's ADVISORY (non-gating)
    #     tauri-build job; the COMBINED-state test runs on the Linux rows only. `custom-protocol`
    #     is exercised only by jobs that first export gui/app/out for compile-time embedding.
issues.title: Justification dropped the "on Linux" qualifier, but the combined-state test is still Linux-only

issues.body:
The comment above the combined-state test still reads 'HDT's feature-on path is compile-covered above; the tests executed in this combined Linux state exercise the federation, ODRL, and forms paths.'

This PR added a dedicated `- name: Test (HDT import, native lane)` step running `cargo test --features hdt` directly above, so HDT is now test-covered in its feature-on state, not merely compile-covered. The drift is in the harmless (understating) direction, but it is the sentence release.yml quotes verbatim as its evidence, so the two files now under-describe the same lane in lockstep.
issues.fix_hint: Reword to: '# Each optional feature is clippied AND tested individually above; this combined Linux state additionally proves the four features co-exist at runtime (federation, ODRL, and forms paths).' Then mirror the correction in release.yml's justification bullet.
issues.title: Stale comment: "HDT's feature-on path is compile-covered above" now understates the coverage this PR added

issues.body:
`tauri-build` (timeout-minutes: 45, continue-on-error: true) previously ran: clippy+build+test on defaults, clippy+test for federation, clippy+test for odrl, plus a Linux-only combined clippy. This PR adds clippy+test for `hdt` and clippy+test for `forms` on every row, and removes `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` from the union clippy so it too runs on all five rows.

Each distinct feature set recompiles the whole dependency graph (hdt pulls sparq-hdt, odrl pulls sparq-policy + sparq-solid, forms pulls oxrdf + sparq-forms), so this roughly doubles the compile work on macos-15-intel / windows-latest / ubuntu-24.04-arm. On a cold cache that could exceed the 45-minute timeout, and because the job is continue-on-error a timeout is silent — so the added coverage may not actually materialise on the slower rows, and release.yml now cites it as evidence.
issues.fix_hint: Either raise `timeout-minutes` for `tauri-build`, or restore `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` on the union clippy (and consider it for the hdt/forms permutations) so the extra compiles land on the rows whose release counterparts are BLOCKING (soft: false) and where the signal is actually load-bearing, leaving macOS/Windows on default-feature clippy/build/test.
issues.title: Union clippy lost its Linux-only guard, adding four full feature-permutation compiles to a 45-minute advisory job on all five rows

verdict.summary:
Both round-3 majors are genuinely resolved in the reviewed tree. (1) The union lane is now `--features hdt,federation,odrl,forms` with `custom-protocol` dropped (fix-hint option (b)), so it no longer hits tauri-codegen's `frontendDist` panic for the gitignored gui/app/out; the omission is explained in-line and release.yml now says honestly that `custom-protocol` is exercised only by jobs that first export gui/app/out. (2) release.yml no longer cites a lane that cannot compile.

Verified against the checkout, not just the diff text: all four stubs (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89) yield the literal 'rebuild the desktop app with' after Rust line-continuation stripping, so the regex matches all four and one missing feature is caught; `productName` is "sparq" (tauri-cli renames sparq-gui -> sparq), so the sparq/sparq-gui candidate loop plus .exe covers every row; the crate has its own `[workspace]`, so gui/src-tauri/target/release is the right path; the guard runs BEFORE installer staging/upload, so a stub-contaminated binary cannot ship; and no frontend string false-positives the regex (streaming-tool.tsx:360's 'Rebuild with' does not match). oxrdf resolves to a single 0.3.3 in gui/src-tauri/Cargo.lock, so the new `forms` lanes should unify cleanly.

What remains is comment drift plus one carried-over minor; no blockers or majors. The most concrete: release.yml's step comment now contradicts itself — the new text says the release enables 'SHACL-derived forms' while the sq-3w29b paragraph 20 lines below still says 'Forms remains opt-in until a release explicitly selects its larger SHACL model stack'. The guard is still negative-only, and gui.yml's 'HDT's feature-on path is compile-covered above' is stale now that a `cargo test --features hdt` lane sits directly above it. This workflow is tag-triggered, so none of it executes on this PR.
